metadata.notes: Integration-authored player salutations bound to thirteen unchanged baseline NPC variants across four existing ordinary adult Greet owners. Baseline NPC wording is not claimed as newly source-certified conversion. No NPC resources, menus, topics, cameras, quests or delivered pairing files changed. Exact fine-tier and real first/familiar guards constrain player voice, not inferred events. Unbound NPC results retain original NPC-only fallback.

reason_definitions.paired: Existing baseline NPC salutation, general advice or figurative attention statement accepts a low-consequence salutation without requiring a claimed purpose or player action. All original conditions and text remain unchanged.
reason_definitions.unguarded_worksite_proximity: NPC wording presumes nearby workstation, tools, material, furniture, safe side or approach geometry not guaranteed by this ordinary greeting owner.
reason_definitions.unguarded_recent_or_current_work: NPC wording presumes actual recent/current task, object state, ongoing work, imminent work interruption or event not guarded by this ordinary greeting owner.
reason_definitions.unguarded_time_or_weather: NPC wording presumes a particular time, recent duration or weather not guarded by this ordinary greeting owner. Rendering the player clock token does not certify the NPC premise.
reason_definitions.unguarded_player_approach_or_equipment: NPC wording presumes player arrival, movement, carried/lowered equipment or observed condition not guaranteed by this ordinary greeting owner.
reason_definitions.unguarded_prior_incident: NPC wording refers to a repeated prior shelving incident; no corresponding recorded-history guard exists in this owner.
reason_definitions.unrepresented_action_or_purpose_reply: NPC wording asks for a specific purpose, explanation, object demonstration, physical action or additional choice. A generic player salutation cannot supply that continuation; no automatic answer/action is authored.

variant_inventory.npc_text: If you need me, speak up. If you need gossip, speak quieter.
Hello. Try not to bring the whole village into this unless it is important.
I have a moment. Not a long one, but a real one.
Stand clear of the <wavy>heat</wavy>. A forge forgives less than I do.
Give the forge room. Armor works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the forge. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
Mind the heat. The forge has no manners today.
Stand clear of the anvil unless you came to learn patience loudly.
Keep your sleeves back. Hot metal makes quick decisions.
Come in carefully. Everything here is either heavy, hot, or judging me.
There you are. I was just near the forge, trying to keep the day sensible.
You caught me before the next little disaster. That is rare timing.
Good timing. I was checking straps before the day found teeth.
Hello. If you smell smoke, that is the work behaving normally.
You caught me between hammer strikes. Speak while the iron waits.
If you need armor, say so before the next plate cools.
Morning. Or afternoon. The work makes the hours blur if I let it.
Morning. I have sparks, dents, and a little time.
Good to see you walking in calmly. That usually means nothing is on fire yet.
Good to see someone walking in without fresh holes in their gear.
Mind the fletching table. Straight arrows do not happen by accident.
Give the fletching table room. Arrow making works better without elbows in the way.
Step carefully near the fletching table. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
Stand clear of the target lane unless you are very confident and very foolish.
Mind the shafts. Straight work dislikes careless elbows.
Come closer from the side, not from downrange.
Hello there. Try not to breathe on the feather pile.
Step around the fletching table and keep your hands friendly.
There you are. I was just near the fletching table, trying to keep the day sensible.
Hello. The feathers are sorted and my patience is mostly intact.
You caught me before the next string test.
Good timing. I was about to argue with the wind.
I have a moment while the glue dries.
The bow is unstrung, so conversation is safer now.
I am listening, but one eye is still checking that shaft.
The range is quiet for now. What do you need?
Good timing. I was about to take a break from the fletching table.
Speak up. The wind has been interrupting all morning.
Good to see you arriving without a target on your back.
If you need arrows, say how many and why.
Welcome. Clean hands make better readers.
Hello there. Do not fold the corners of anything alive or paper.
You look like a question with boots.
I can spare a short chapter of attention.
Mind the lectern. It has heard better questions than most people ask.
Give the lectern room. Record keeping works better without elbows in the way.
Step carefully near the lectern. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
Lower your voice a little. The shelves are dramatic today.
Mind the lectern. It holds grudges through splinters.
Come in quietly or at least thoughtfully.
Stand away from the open ink and near your better judgment.
There you are. I was just near the lectern, trying to keep the day sensible.
You caught me between pages, which is safer than between arguments.
The books are settled. Let us see if people can match them.
Good timing. I was losing a debate with a footnote.
I am listening, though the margin was speaking first.
Good timing. I was about to take a break from the library.
I have a moment, provided nobody has shelved farming under danger again.
Hello. If you borrowed something, begin with honesty.
If you need an answer, tell me whether you want quick or correct.
If you need me, speak up. If you need gossip, speak quieter.
Hello. Try not to bring the whole village into this unless it is important.
I have a moment. Not a long one, but a real one.
Keep clear of the stonecutter. It does not care who started the conversation.
Give the stonecutter room. It is sharper than this conversation needs to be.
Stand wide of the stonecutter. It never asks who leaned in first.
Mind the dust. It travels better than most merchants.
Hello. Stand clear of the stone unless you know where it wants to fall.
Careful near the cutter. It has no patience for fingers.
Come closer, but not under that block.
Welcome. If you lean on that stack, we both learn something bad.
Hello there. Try not to kick the guide line.
Stand where the floor is finished and tell me what you need.
There you are. I was just near the stonecutter, trying to keep the day sensible.
You caught me before the next little disaster. That is rare timing.
You caught me between measurements.
Good timing. The mortar is resting and so am I, briefly.
I have a moment before the next corner demands proof.
The stone is steady today. I appreciate the example.
Speak up. The chisel has been arguing with me.
I was checking level. People are harder to keep straight.
The wall can wait one breath. What is it?
Morning. Or afternoon. The work makes the hours blur if I let it.
Good to see you walking in calmly. That usually means nothing is on fire yet.
Good to see you arriving without loose rubble.
If you need me, speak up. If you need gossip, speak quieter.
Hello. Try not to bring the whole village into this unless it is important.
I have a moment. Not a long one, but a real one.
Mind the table. Good tools begin with nobody bumping my elbow.
Give the smithing table room. Tools work better without elbows in the way.
Careful by the smithing table. I prefer greetings to bandages.
Mind the handles. They are sorted by purpose and irritation.
Stand clear of the grindstone unless you enjoy sparks in your story.
Come closer, but leave the sharp things where they are.
Welcome. Do not lean on the finished tools.
The table is full, but I can make room for words.
Stand by the safe side and tell me what you need.
There you are. I was just near the smithing table, trying to keep the day sensible.
You caught me before the next little disaster. That is rare timing.
You caught me between edges.
Good timing. The metal is cooling and so is my temper.
I have a moment before the next repair becomes urgent.
Speak up. The grindstone has been louder than sense today.
I was checking balance. People could use that too.
You have my attention until the next handle cracks.
Morning. Or afternoon. The work makes the hours blur if I let it.
Good to see you walking in calmly. That usually means nothing is on fire yet.
Good to see you carrying tools instead of excuses.
Hello. If something broke, show me before explaining why it was not your fault.
Hello there. If you need a tool, name the job first.
Mind the grindstone. It has no patience for wandering fingers.
Give the grindstone room. Steel works better without elbows in the way.
Step carefully near the grindstone. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
If you need an edge fixed, speak up. If you brought gossip, keep it away from the wheel.
Keep clear of the edge work.
Stand away from the grindstone unless sparks improve your mood.
Come closer slowly and keep your hands sensible.
Welcome. Do not touch anything that looks ready to object.
Stand on the safe side and tell me what you need.
There you are. I was just near the grindstone, trying to keep the day sensible.
You caught me between blades. That is the safest time to interrupt.
I have a moment before the steel heats. Make it count.
You caught me while the steel is cooling.
Good timing. The blade is quiet for the moment.
I have a moment before the next edge needs arguing with.
The forge is hot and the day is sharper than I like.
Speak up. The grindstone has been telling the same story all morning.
I was checking balance. People rarely pass as easily.
You have my attention until the steel asks for it back.
Morning. Or afternoon. The forge makes the hours blur together.
Good to see you walking in calmly. That usually means no one brought me a <gradient:gold:red><pulse>broken blade</pulse></gradient>.
Good to see you with your weapon lowered.
Hello. Set any weapon down before you explain what went wrong.
Hello. If you brought a weapon, set it down gently.
Hello there. If this is about repairs, show me the damage.

metadata.optional_context: Sixteen upper-tier goodwill alternatives use actual <time> (morning/afternoon/evening/night). They express hope, not a verified pleasant day. Four familiar actual-known-name alternatives use <villager>. Every exact binding retains two plain alternatives. No questions, admissions, promises, requested physical actions, weather assertions or claimed job are authored.
